cells.why: The developer site documents Docusign's MCP server, with prerequisites.
Docusign publishes OpenAPI files, and the GitHub repository holding them is public.
Docusign Connect is documented as a webhook service for eSignature events.
Every endpoint can be tested in test mode, even from a free account.
API and app plan prices are published ($75 and $15 a month tiers).
A help article says Relay does not offer a public API.
A read-only AI connector exists but is in beta for a small group of customers.
API tokens carry documented scopes that set their level of access.
The MCP server is documented but labeled beta.
Every developer profile gets a sandbox company automatically.
The pricing page lists monthly prices for each plan.
A sandbox exists, but access comes through a sales representative.
No pricing page; the only call to action is Contact Sales.
The EIN application is a browser tool; no API is documented.
Anyone eligible applies online and gets an EIN in minutes, with no call.
The filing system is browser-only; no API page exists.
Filing is by upload or browser services; no API is offered.
The page claims a flat fee but shows no amount.
The vendor says it offers APIs for integrations but shows no public documentation.
A public MCP tool directory with a catalog and connection steps.
